profile.name: Jiangyu Liu
profile.subtitle: Undergraduate, Department of Automation, Tsinghua University

aboutMe: I am an undergraduate in the Department of Automation at Tsinghua University, currently working in Ning Ding's research group.

I am especially interested in using agents to control robots: how they can understand tasks, plan actions, and interact with the physical world. I am also interested in reinforcement learning (RL), vision-language-action models (VLA), world models, and 3D vision, and how these approaches can help robots perceive their surroundings, anticipate changes, and learn to accomplish tasks through interaction.

I am still at the beginning of my research journey and enjoy exploring new questions through learning and hands-on work. Outside research, I enjoy table tennis and volunteering. Feel free to reach out for a game, a meal, or a chat about research and volunteer activities!

items.title: Anyverse Dynamics | Algorithm Intern (Mar–Jun 2026)
items.text: Gained hands-on experience fine-tuning π0 with LoRA and working with embodied AI training pipelines. Worked on world action model (WAM) development and inference optimization, drawing on Fast-WAM and Motus. Analyzed the Motus inference pipeline, iterated on acceleration experiments, and completed technical validation, building familiarity with WAMs and research engineering workflows.

items.title: DISCOVER Robotics | Algorithm Intern (Jun–Sep 2026)
items.text: Contributed to foundation model development and 3D perception. Integrated motion representations from ZipMo into Fast-WAM to improve generalization across tasks and environments. Designed and evaluated a tokenizer for stereo visual inputs, exploring how binocular geometry can support embodied perception and action modeling.

items.title: Student Research Training (SRT)
items.text: Contributed to a robotic system for multimodal collaborative perception and concurrent task execution. Gained experience with robot system operation and the research process from initial design to deployment on physical robots.

items.title: ATEC 2026
items.text: Participated in the AI and Robotics Real-World Extreme Challenge, working on robot vision, data tools, and SLAM-based navigation. Used YOLO11-seg for nine-class instance segmentation (mask mAP50–95: 87.01%), with SAM2 and FoundationPose for annotation propagation and 6D pose estimation. Built a desktop application integrating RGB-D data collection, annotation review, model training, and live recognition. Using ROS 2, Nav2, SLAM Toolbox, and Gazebo, implemented mapping, localization, RPP path tracking, two-goal navigation with obstacle avoidance, and SDK2 control integration for the Unitree A2+P7. Built a repeatable navigation simulation setup and gained experience testing on physical robots.
